In 2026-01, the citywide corridor network recorded a mean congestion score of 29.8 (climbed by +2.0 points vs previous month, n=1,860 observation records). Peak friction concentrated along Hinjewadi-Swargate during the 18-20 slot (n=372 corridor readings), with 9.7% of all slots in High or Very High congestion bands. Weekday travel times averaged 29.5 versus 30.6 on weekends (gap of -1.0 points, n=1,320 weekday records). The primary friction drivers were hotspot (55.0), construction (17.3), metro (10.7), while MAD analysis identified 28 corridor-level anomalous peak events across 155 route-days.

📅 Month: 2026-04 Executive Intelligence

In 2026-04, the citywide corridor network recorded a mean congestion score of 38.6 (climbed by +1.7 points vs previous month, n=1,935 observation records). Peak friction concentrated along Hinjewadi-Swargate during the 18-20 slot (n=387 corridor readings), with 17.5% of all slots in High or Very High congestion bands. Weekday travel times averaged 40.8 versus 32.1 on weekends (gap of +8.7 points, n=1,455 weekday records). The primary friction drivers were transit (6.8), hotspot (6.4), construction (5.8), while MAD analysis identified 20 corridor-level anomalous peak events across 150 route-days.

📅 Month: 2026-05 Executive Intelligence

In 2026-05, the citywide corridor network recorded a mean congestion score of 35.2 (eased by -3.4 points vs previous month, n=2,100 observation records). Peak friction concentrated along Katraj-Kondhwa during the 18-20 slot (n=420 corridor readings), with 9.3% of all slots in High or Very High congestion bands. Weekday travel times averaged 36.0 versus 33.7 on weekends (gap of +2.2 points, n=1,380 weekday records). The primary friction drivers were construction (6.4), diversion (5.8), hotspot (2.8), while MAD analysis identified 52 corridor-level anomalous peak events across 155 route-days.

📅 Month: 2026-06 Executive Intelligence

In 2026-06, the citywide corridor network recorded a mean congestion score of 43.9 (climbed by +8.7 points vs previous month, n=2,036 observation records). Peak friction concentrated along Katraj-Kondhwa during the 08-10 slot (n=360 corridor readings), with 18.1% of all slots in High or Very High congestion bands. Weekday travel times averaged 45.3 versus 40.2 on weekends (gap of +5.1 points, n=1,488 weekday records). The primary friction drivers were weather (7.4), construction (5.8), diversion (4.8), while MAD analysis identified 95 corridor-level anomalous peak events across 170 route-days.

Weekday travel times averaged 46.3 versus 43.3 on weekends (gap of +3.0 points, n=1,932 weekday records). The primary friction drivers were weather (8.0), construction (4.8), diversion (4.0), while MAD analysis identified 140 corridor-level anomalous peak events across 217 route-days.

📅 Month: 2026-08 Executive Intelligence

In 2026-08, the citywide corridor network recorded a mean congestion score of 44.4 (eased by -1.1 points vs previous month, n=2,604 observation records). Peak friction concentrated along Swargate-Katraj during the 08-10 slot (n=372 corridor readings), with 21.2% of all slots in High or Very High congestion bands. Weekday travel times averaged 44.7 versus 43.7 on weekends (gap of +1.1 points, n=1,764 weekday records). The primary friction drivers were construction (7.6), diversion (5.3), weather (5.1), while MAD analysis identified 138 corridor-level anomalous peak events across 217 route-days.

📅 Month: 2026-09 Executive Intelligence

In 2026-09, the citywide corridor network recorded a mean congestion score of 55.3 (climbed by +10.9 points vs previous month, n=2,494 observation records). Peak friction concentrated along Swargate-Katraj during the 08-10 slot (n=356 corridor readings), with 45.9% of all slots in High or Very High congestion bands. Weekday travel times averaged 55.8 versus 54.1 on weekends (gap of +1.7 points, n=1,822 weekday records). The primary friction drivers were festival (12.4), construction (9.3), weather (9.1), while MAD analysis identified 176 corridor-level anomalous peak events across 210 route-days.

📅 Month: 2026-10 Executive Intelligence

In 2026-10, the citywide corridor network recorded a mean congestion score of 39.2 (eased by -16.1 points vs previous month, n=2,604 observation records). Peak friction concentrated along Swargate-Katraj during the 08-10 slot (n=372 corridor readings), with 16.6% of all slots in High or Very High congestion bands. Weekday travel times averaged 39.4 versus 38.9 on weekends (gap of +0.4 points, n=1,848 weekday records). The primary friction drivers were construction (11.9), transit (8.7), hotspot (8.4), while MAD analysis identified 117 corridor-level anomalous peak events across 217 route-days.

📅 Month: 2026-11 Executive Intelligence

In 2026-11, the citywide corridor network recorded a mean congestion score of 44.0 (climbed by +4.8 points vs previous month, n=1,260 observation records). Peak friction concentrated along Swargate-Katraj during the 18-20 slot (n=180 corridor readings), with 25.6% of all slots in High or Very High congestion bands. Weekday travel times averaged 44.5 versus 43.0 on weekends (gap of +1.6 points, n=840 weekday records). The primary friction drivers were construction (12.7), transit (9.6), diversion (9.2), while MAD analysis identified 76 corridor-level anomalous peak events across 105 route-days.
